paragraphs: Friend, this passage is basically God handing out the instruction manual for the offerings, and He doesn't skip a single detail. Where the ashes go, who eats what, how long the meat can sit. I think the big idea is that God cares about how He is approached, and He tells His people exactly how. Nobody has to guess, and nobody has to wonder whether they did it right.

And look at what He says about the altar: "The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished." (Leviticus 6:13) That's the heart of it. The priests are on duty morning after morning, and God provides for them too, giving them "a permanent portion" (Leviticus 7:34). The offerings were holy, and the one who served at the altar was cared for. That tells me God takes worship seriously and takes care of those who serve Him.

So what does that mean for you, baker? It means God's holiness is real, and so is His provision. He tells us what He wants, and He is generous to those who serve Him. When I stand at my oven, I want to stay ready and do it the way He asked, because He is worth that kind of care. Keep your fire going, friend!
